From the owner
Kitchen Remodeling for Better Everyday Function A kitchen can have plenty of space and still feel difficult to use when the layout, storage, and work surfaces do not support everyday routines. Kitchen remodeling provides an opportunity to correct those issues while creating a more comfortable place for cooking and gathering. Cabinet placement can improve access to cookware and pantry items, while a well-planned island adds valuable prep space and seating. Countertops, lighting, appliances, electrical access, and ventilation also need to work together. Careful planning helps reduce unnecessary movement between cooking, cleaning, and storage areas while making better use of the available space. An island cooktop also makes proper ventilation an important part of the design. A substantial overhead range hood can help control heat, smoke, and cooking odors while leaving surrounding walls available for cabinet storage. Light cabinetry can keep the room feeling open, stone counters provide practical work surfaces, and a tile backsplash protects areas exposed to everyday cooking. We also consider walking clearance, drawer access, seating placement, appliance doors, and how each work zone connects. Planning a kitchen remodel and want a layout that works better for your household? Contact Crow Construction to discuss your ideas and renovation needs.

From the owner
Project Spotlight: Bathroom Transformation in Sturgis, SD A recent project in Sturgis, South Dakota, highlights the importance of addressing hidden bathroom issues before they cause structural issues. Homeowners Tim and Marcia were dealing with an aging, cracked fiberglass shower unit that had begun to leak, posing a continuous threat of water damage to their flooring. To resolve the issue permanently, the old fixture was completely stripped away and replaced with a modern, durable shower and tub system. The new setup focuses on both long-term reliability and updated aesthetics, featuring: Subway Tile Design: A crisp, white subway tile pattern that opens up the room and creates a brighter environment. Built-In Convenience: Two integrated corner shelving units that provide sturdy storage for everyday essentials. Safety & Hardware: A sleek, modern grab bar for improved accessibility, paired with matching brushed metal hardware. Space Optimization: A curved shower rod to maximize space and comfort. The completed project successfully turned a high-maintenance problem area into a beautiful, leak-free sanctuary designed to stand the test of time. This case study demonstrates how modern, high-quality materials can completely refresh a residential space while providing long-term peace of mind against water leaks.

From the owner
For a mid-range kitchen renovation, homeowners should generally budget between $15,000 and $25,000. For a larger kitchen or a project involving extensive changes, a reasonable starting budget may be $30,000 to $45,000. These are planning ranges—not guaranteed prices. Final cost depends on the kitchen’s size, cabinet type, countertops, appliances, demolition, plumbing and electrical work, permits, and the condition of the existing space. Labor commonly represents about 20% to 35% of the total remodeling cost. This may include demolition, cabinet and countertop installation, plumbing, electrical work, flooring, painting, finish carpentry, and project coordination. Moving sinks, appliances, walls, gas lines, or electrical circuits generally costs more than keeping the existing layout. Cabinet refacing may be worth considering when the cabinet boxes remain sound and the current layout works well. When storage, cabinet condition, or layout needs major improvement, replacement or custom cabinetry may provide better long-term value. A useful kitchen remodeling estimate should be based on accurate measurements, an actual design, selected materials, and a clearly defined scope of work. Fresno Cabinet Outlet helps Central Valley homeowners compare cabinet refacing, preassembled cabinets, custom cabinetry, countertops, and complete remodeling options before deciding where their budget will provide the greatest value. Prices vary by project and material selections.

From the owner
Is Masonite Siding Still Made? Here's What Birmingham Homeowners Should Know No. Masonite hardboard siding was discontinued in the late 1990s after class-action lawsuits over moisture damage. The Masonite company still exists, but it makes doors now, not siding. Many homes in Hoover, Pelham and the Birmingham area still have the original Masonite. If yours does, look for these signs: ✔ Swollen or bulging boards, mostly near the bottom edge ✔ Soft spots, rot or mushroom-like growth ✔ Paint that peels again soon after repainting ✔ Cracks around nails, windows and trim Because the product is discontinued, a matching replacement board is hard to find. Patching often leaves a visible mismatch, and the damage can keep spreading behind the wall. Your options: • Repair small areas using a closely matched modern profile • Replace the siding with LP SmartSide engineered wood or James Hardie fiber cement. Both are built to resist Alabama's humidity, termites and storms. HRS has repaired and replaced siding across the Birmingham metro since 1976. We'll check your siding and tell you plainly whether a repair will last or it's time to replace. 📍 Serving Hoover, Pelham, Vestavia Hills, Homewood and Greater Birmingham 👉 Book your free siding inspection today.

Bathroom finishes have to survive water, humidity, and daily cleaning. Porcelain tile outperforms natural stone on bathroom floors because it does not need sealing and resists staining. Check the slip rating on any floor tile going into a wet area. Quartz handles vanity tops well since it is non porous. Solid wood vanities hold up better than particleboard in a humid room, and a properly sized exhaust fan vented outside, not into the attic, protects everything else you just installed. Beautiful materials in a poorly ventilated bathroom fail early. Visit our Pasadena showroom to compare bathroom materials in person.

From the owner
A properly installed sump pump does quiet, important work under your home, and most homeowners never think about it until something goes wrong. That blue basin in your basement floor is your first line of defense against water buildup. When groundwater rises, the pump kicks on and sends it safely away through the discharge line. With fall rain soaking Erie and the ground staying wet heading into winter, making sure that system is sealed, connected, and running right matters. Our team handles the full picture as a local waterproofing contractor: 🔹 Sump pump installation, repair, and maintenance 🔹 Basement leak repair when water finds another way in 🔹 Crawl space repair to control moisture below the home 🔹 Full basement waterproofing systems sized to your property We have been a waterproofing company Erie County homeowners can count on since 1982, and we always match the solution to the actual problem, not a generic fix. Not sure when your pump was last checked? Reach out to schedule a free estimate and we will take a look.

From the owner
Permits and approvals are what trip up a whole house remodel, especially once fall schedules get tight and winter weather starts closing in. Before we swing a hammer we map the paperwork: building permits, trade permits (plumbing, electric, HVAC), and any structural sign-off if walls, beams, or stair layouts change. If you’re in a condo or co-op, the building packet can be its own job. We pull the alteration agreement, insurance requirements, elevator rules, work hours, debris handling, and the board review timeline. Brownstones bring their own limits too: shared walls, party-wall protections, and neighbor notice if we’re doing anything that affects structure, noise, or access. Street and sidewalk logistics matter in Hoboken NJ. If we need a dumpster, materials staging, or a lane of curb space, we plan it early so the job is not waiting on approvals. Want us to look at your place and lay out the permit path?

Selecting the Right Flooring for Your Remodel: Choosing new flooring seems like a design decision until you start comparing materials. Hardwood, engineered wood, luxury vinyl plank, porcelain tile, and natural stone can all look beautiful in a finished room. They do not, however, perform the same way in a busy kitchen, a second-floor bedroom, or a basement. For a home remodel in Northern Virginia, the right floor needs to do more than match your cabinets and paint. It should fit the home's architecture, handle how the room is used, work with the conditions beneath it, and still look appropriate years after the renovation. Before choosing a color or plank width, understand what each flooring material does well, where it has limitations, and how it will connect with the rest of your home.
